name: Paper Dosa
steps: Wash and soak rice, urad dal and fenugreek for 5 hours. Grind with the measured water to a smooth batter, cover loosely and ferment overnight until visibly risen.
Stir in salt without flattening the batter. Heat a broad seasoned griddle; a drop of water should dance and evaporate quickly.

Heat the largest well-seasoned griddle available until a drop of water evaporates at once. Pour a small ladle of batter in the centre and spread in wide, fast concentric circles, making an unusually long, nearly translucent sheet.
Drizzle a little oil over the surface and edge. Cook over medium heat for 3–5 minutes, until the whole underside is crisp golden and its edges lift freely; do not flip or add a filling.
Lift carefully with a long spatula, fold loosely and transfer immediately to a broad plate. Serve with warm sambar and coconut chutney; never stack paper dosas because steam destroys their crispness.
tips: Paper dosa depends on an exceptionally thin spread and a broad hot griddle.
passiveTime: Soak grains for 5 hours and ferment overnight.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
